feedback: When your counting-on reaches the amount paid, confirm success: 'You've counted on to 50p — the 15p of change you built (10p + 5p), added to the 35p price, rebuilds the amount paid.' (Note the change coins total 15p; it is the running total counted on from the price that reaches 50p.)
If one coin too many goes in, show the running total overshooting the amount paid (past 50p) and invite the child to remove a coin and recount up.
If the running total is still short, point to the remaining gap: 'Counting on from 35p you've reached 40p — how much more to reach 50p?'

Optional live supports that make the mechanism visible: a running-total bar that starts at the price (35p) and rises with each coin to the amount paid (50p), and an empty number line on which each jump (+5, +10) draws itself from 35 up to 50.
activities.intendedInsight: Change is the DISTANCE travelled from the price up to the amount paid — it is the total of the jumps you make when counting up (here 5p + 10p = 15p), not a take-away you have to work out on paper. The coins themselves record how the change was reached.
learnerActions: Set up a shop: a toy priced 35p, a 50p coin to pay with, and a pot of mixed coins.
Count UP aloud from the price to the amount paid, placing a coin into a change tray at each step: '35… (put in a 5p) 40… (put in a 10p) 50'.
State the change as the coins you built: 'The change is 15p — a 10p and a 5p.'
Check by counting the change back onto the price to confirm it rebuilds the amount paid (35p + 15p = 50p).
Repeat with other friendly prices (e.g. 45p paid with 50p gives 5p), then extend to the source worked example 27p paid with 50p, counting 27→30→50 to give 3p + 20p = 23p.
activities.title: Give change at a role-play market stall (count up with coins)

feedback: Confirm when the count-up reaches the price exactly: '15 up to 20 is one jump of 5p — you need 5p more.'
If the child adds 15 + 20, re-anchor: 'You already have 15p; count on from there up to 20p to see what's missing.'
activities.intendedInsight: Finding change and finding 'how much more I need' (missing addend) are one idea: closing the gap by counting up between two amounts.
learnerActions: Set a toy priced 20p and give the child 15p.
Ask: 'How much MORE do you need to buy this?'
Count UP from what you have to the price: '15… (add a 5p) 20' and name the shortfall as 5p.
Line this up against a change task: notice that finding the shortfall and finding change are the same counting-up move, just started from a different amount.
activities.title: 'How much more do I need?' — the same gap read the other way

feedback: When the child checks totals: 'A fistful of pennies can be worth less than one coin — it's the value that counts, not the number.'
Praise finding several coin combinations that make the same value.
activities.intendedInsight: Money is judged by total value, not by how many coins there are; many small coins can be worth less than one larger coin.
learnerActions: Lay the child's handful of small coins beside a single 10p and 5p.
Count the total VALUE of each set and compare, e.g. show that ten 1p coins are worth less than one 20p.
Make the SAME value (e.g. 15p) with different coin combinations (10p + 5p; 5p + 5p + 5p; 10p + 2p + 2p + 1p).
activities.title: Value, not number of coins
